prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators, from the quantum spin Hall state to three-dimensional topological materials

statement.case_for: B041 is the only shortlisted case that combines a clear conceptual origin with unambiguous experimental fingerprints. Band topology with spin-orbit coupling gave a new classification of insulators, the quantum spin Hall edge channels were measured in HgTe wells, and three-dimensional topological insulators were mapped with ARPES. The discovery is at the centre, not only the idea. It has two decades of independent confirmation across many materials and probes, a stable interpretation, and it has reorganised condensed matter and materials research. It also has the broadest opening support in this run, with four first-place rankings and five top-three rankings, though I do not treat that as a measure of merit. A theory, first-experiment and 3D-materials trio covers the three steps that define the field, and the maturity argument is stronger here than for any rival: this is overdue rather than premature.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Kane and Mele wrote the Z2 theory together, so leaving Mele out of a Kane, Molenkamp, Hasan configuration separates a joint theoretical contribution, and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe prediction that guided Molenkamp's experiment lies outside the credited names. Four colleagues prefer Kane, Mele and Molenkamp as the cleanest set. B041 also overlaps heavily with B029, so the committee must choose one framing, and Hasan's priority for the 3D materials has to be weighed against parallel theory by Fu, Kane and Mele, Moore, Balents and others. If the credit cannot be defended with only three names, the case weakens.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks B041 first and prefers Kane, Mele and Molenkamp as the cleanest configuration from the supplied names, treating Hasan's 3D work as a strong claim that does not fit in three slots.
responses.response: I agree that Mele is the hardest omission and I take that seriously. Where I differ is on what the prize is for. The quantum spin Hall edge states in HgTe and the 3D materials seen by ARPES are the experimental discoveries, and a theory-only pair would cite two names for the Z2 idea and one for the experiment. Dropping Hasan leaves the 3D phase, which made topological insulators a materials class, without a credited experimentalist. I would reopen Mele versus Hasan if colleagues think the Kane-Mele paper carries the prize, but I hold that the experimental side should have two slots.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks B029 first with Kane, Molenkamp and Xue, treating the quantum anomalous Hall effect as part of a theory-plus-two-experiments trio and leaving out Mele and Hasan.
responses.response: B029 is a fair framing and shares my core of Kane and Molenkamp, so the disagreement is narrow. I still prefer Hasan to Xue. The quantum anomalous Hall effect is a real experimental achievement, but it is a later realisation that depends on the topological-insulator concept and on magnetic doping of materials like those Hasan's school helped establish. Making it the third pillar would shift the citation toward a downstream application of topology. I would keep B029 as a fallback if the committee wants to avoid the Mele and Hasan question and prefers a narrower, better-defined experimental story.

responses.point: Kroll ranks B013 first: optical lattice clocks reach about 1e-18 fractional uncertainty with a clean two-name credit of Katori and Ye, and the redefinition of the second is under discussion.
responses.response: B013 has the cleanest attribution on the shortlist and I rate it highly, because precision measurement gives real clues about nature through tests of constants and relativistic geodesy. My hesitation is that part of the conceptual ground, optical frequency metrology and the comb, was recognised in 2005, and Ye's weight across other candidates raises configuration questions. Compared with topological insulators, it is a more incremental advance within an established programme than the creation of a new class of matter. I would not block it and keep it as an alternative.

responses.point: Pearce ranks B018 first as a decisive, clean reactor measurement of theta13 that opened leptonic CP-violation searches, and notes the Daya Bay versus accelerator credit balance across Luk, Wang and Nishikawa.
responses.response: I accept that theta13 was a decisive and clean measurement, and a real discovery in nature. My difficulty is the credit. It is a collaboration-scale result with several reactor experiments and T2K, so three names would pick leaders rather than discoverers in a way that is hard to defend, and the 2015 oscillation prize already covers the underlying phenomenon. It had one first-place ranking and no other support in the opening ballots. I would need to hear a concrete argument for why these three people, and not their collaborations' other leaders, carry the credit before moving it up.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks B013 first and B014 second, and notes that B041 is mature but that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe state, with Hasan, Moore, Balents, Fu and Roy central to the 3D theory.
responses.response: Lindroth's point about the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal is the best argument against the credited set, and I do not have a good answer to it within the supplied names. I can only say that the committee works with the names it is given and that Molenkamp's measurement was the experimental discovery. We should record in our deliberation that the theory credit around HgTe is incomplete, and that is a reason for care in the citation wording rather than a reason to downgrade the field.

uncertainties: Whether Mele or Hasan should take the third slot, and whether the committee prefers a theory-heavy Kane, Mele, Molenkamp set.
Whether B041 or B029 is the better framing, given that they share Kane and Molenkamp and differ on Mele, Hasan and Xue.
Priority claims for the HgTe prediction and the 3D theory sit outside the credited names, and I rely on memory of the chronology without verification.
Whether the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize and recent condensed-matter awards change the committee's appetite for another condensed-matter topic in 2026.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My connections are David Gross, Hector Rubinstein, Thomas Van Riet and the Uppsala theory group, and none is credited on any shortlisted ballot. My string theory and cosmology field is not among the shortlisted candidates.
